raw_response: {"sentences":[{"text":"From Fraunces Tavern, make your way onto Wall Street — about a nine-minute walk.","source_id":"GLUE_NAV","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":3},{"text":"Take a second to think about where you've been.","source_id":"GLUE_REFLECTION","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":3},{"text":"Inside Fraunces Tavern, Washington gave his Farewell to the Troops, and Hamilton set up his very first Office of the Treasury.","source_id":"GLUE_REFLECTION","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":3},{"text":"The Sons of Liberty had gathered in that same building to plot evicting the British — and in 1975 the FALN bombed it, killing four.","source_id":"GLUE_REFLECTION","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":3},{"text":"You began the morning at Bowling Green, the city's first official park, laid out in 1733.","source_id":"GLUE_REFLECTION","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":3},{"text":"Now start at 1 Liberty Plaza, the U.S. Steel Building, which quietly holds a record.","source_id":"38110857-d9f1-4e19-957f-3b2926fde39f","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"The tallest building ever demolished once stood right here — the Singer Building.","source_id":"38110857-d9f1-4e19-957f-3b2926fde39f","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"When it came down, the grief wasn't quite what New York felt when Pennsylvania Station was slaughtered in 1963, but its long place in the skyline still brought tears of rage.","source_id":"38110857-d9f1-4e19-957f-3b2926fde39f","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"And when crews dug the foundations here from 1979 to 1982, they turned up three-century-old fragments of the Lovelace Tavern, once housed nearby.","source_id":"a0c3e193-82b0-4dce-bc09-e75bc79da027","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"Head west to 14 Wall, the Bankers Trust Building.","source_id":"67e3cd7a-c7d8-46ed-abd2-427753a28e46","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"Bankers Trust is gone, but Trowbridge and Livingston's pyramidal crown remains, modeled on antiquity's Mausoleum at Halicarnassus and still one of the great pinnacles in a city bathed in sumptuous finishing touches.","source_id":"67e3cd7a-c7d8-46ed-abd2-427753a28e46","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"J. P. Morgan even shacked up beneath that pyramid so he could watch his own building rise across the street.","source_id":"67e3cd7a-c7d8-46ed-abd2-427753a28e46","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"For years the pyramid was the bank's logo, though — such is the depth of these downtown canyons — you can't see it from Wall Street itself.","source_id":"67e3cd7a-c7d8-46ed-abd2-427753a28e46","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"Duck inside for the bronze lobby gates, cast with the enterprises of capitalism: metallurgy, shipping, mining, agriculture, and power.","source_id":"67e3cd7a-c7d8-46ed-abd2-427753a28e46","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"At 22 William, between Beaver and Exchange Place, is the City Bank Farmers' Trust Building of 1931.","source_id":"426c7324-0a3b-4da4-bdfd-c5e50db78009","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"Its irregular site pushed the architects to experiment, so it pivots off the grid as if it's about to blast off — always a curiosity in these canyons.","source_id":"426c7324-0a3b-4da4-bdfd-c5e50db78009","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"The bronze doors are the showpiece, filled with trains, boats, and airplanes, and inside there's more than forty kinds of marble laced with nickel and copper.","source_id":"426c7324-0a3b-4da4-bdfd-c5e50db78009","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"Cross to the west side of Broadway, where No. 25 was Cunard's central ticket office.","source_id":"c7a39989-c48b-45a1-9955-2abe482968b1","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"Cunard led the pack among the era's steamship lines, and in 1921 put up this building for the firm that ran the fastest, most luxurious liners in the world.","source_id":"c7a39989-c48b-45a1-9955-2abe482968b1","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"In the age of expensive cruises and mass immigration, that was huge business — so much so that this bottom stretch of Broadway went by a nickname, Steamship Row.","source_id":"c7a39989-c48b-45a1-9955-2abe482968b1","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"Step inside, but not on a Sunday, for spectacular wall frescoes and maps tracing the old Cunard routes.","source_id":"c7a39989-c48b-45a1-9955-2abe482968b1","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"Now look up Broadway to No. 26, on the corner of Beaver, crowned with a cast-iron oil burner.","source_id":"8639b9ba-68de-4efb-9e78-aa54b45a212d","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"That lantern tells you exactly what the building was for: it housed Standard Oil, John D. Rockefeller's monopolistic firm.","source_id":"8639b9ba-68de-4efb-9e78-aa54b45a212d","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"But by the time this tower went up in 1924, the flame was long out — in 1911 the U.S. Supreme Court had ordered the Standard Oil Holding Company dissolved and its directors stripped of control over the subsidiaries.","source_id":"8639b9ba-68de-4efb-9e78-aa54b45a212d","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"The offices lingered here until the 1930s, when the firm moved uptown to the new Rockefeller Center.","source_id":"8639b9ba-68de-4efb-9e78-aa54b45a212d","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"And long before any of it, in 1796, another financial giant lived on this very spot — Alexander Hamilton kept his town residence here.","source_id":"8639b9ba-68de-4efb-9e78-aa54b45a212d","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"On the corner of Pearl and Whitehall, No. 33 houses NASDAQ, the National Association of Securities Dealers, though unlike the Stock Exchange its visitor center sits up in Times Square, not here.","source_id":"c73442c1-c107-440c-9f3c-81955c39f721","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"The real story is across the street to the south, where the Whitehall Induction Center once stood — the place Arlo Guthrie immortalized in \"Alice's Restaurant\" as where he was \"injected, inspected, detected, infected, neglected, and selected,\" and where, in 1967, during Stop the Draft Week, they arrested Benjamin Spock, the famed baby doctor turned antiwar leader, alongside the poet Allen Ginsberg.","source_id":"c73442c1-c107-440c-9f3c-81955c39f721","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"End at 55 Wall Street, a building born from disaster.","source_id":"bce65fe5-0d61-4082-9ac8-388aee069528","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"The Great Fire of 1835 took seven hundred buildings, the Merchants Exchange among them, and Isaiah Rogers designed this to replace it in 1842.","source_id":"bce65fe5-0d61-4082-9ac8-388aee069528","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"It served as the U.S. Custom House from 1863 to 1899, then later as a branch of Citibank.","source_id":"bce65fe5-0d61-4082-9ac8-388aee069528","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"Watch how the columns stack — a lower Ionic colonnade from 1842, each shaft a single block of stone, working hand in glove with a Corinthian row added seventy years above it.","source_id":"bce65fe5-0d61-4082-9ac8-388aee069528","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3},{"text":"Inside, the lobby runs 198 feet long and 132 feet high, and holds the largest display of Wedgwood china in the world around its central chandelier.","source_id":"bce65fe5-0d61-4082-9ac8-388aee069528","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":3}]}
